proposals.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (well above 2 eV), electronically insulating lithium phosphate. Its P-O framework is oxidatively stable near 4 V vs Li, so it should block cathode-side oxidation of the sulfide. It is also a known, widely used coating layer and is chemically compatible with the PS4 framework of Li6PS5Cl. This is a first, exploratory pick, so I chose one polymorph before testing the other.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (well above 2 eV), electronically insulating lithium phosphate. Its P-O framework is oxidatively stable near 4 V vs Li, so it should block cathode-side oxidation of the sulfide. It is also a known, widely used coating layer and is chemically compatible with the PS4 framework of Li6PS5Cl. This is a first, exploratory pick, so I chose one polymorph before testing the other.

LiF is a wide-gap, highly electronegative and thermodynamically stable Li salt. Its anion is already fully reduced and resists oxidation, so it should be chemically inert toward the PS4/Cl framework of Li6PS5Cl. A fluoride should also avoid the P2O5/SO2 oxidation products that gave the phosphate its high contact penalty. Using a different family (halide) tests whether a non-oxygen, non-reactive coating can lower the penalty below 0.05 eV/atom.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (phosphate) gave a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/atom (bin 16) from reaction with the sulfide to form P2O5, SCl4 and SO2. This suggests the oxygen-containing phosphate reacts with the electrolyte, so a fluoride-based coating is worth testing.

proposal.hypothesis: LiNbO3 is a d0 Nb5+ oxide with a wide gap, and it is the classic sulfide-compatible cathode coating. Nb5+ is hard to reduce, so the oxide should resist reaction with the PS4/Cl framework better than Li3PO4 or LiF, which both formed P2O5, SO2 and SCl species in contact with the electrolyte.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (penalty 0.310, bin 15) and LiF (penalty 0.337, bin 16) both reacted with Li6PS5Cl to form P2O5, SO2 and chlorosulfur species, so a non-phosphate, non-fluoride oxide is the next family to test.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2ZnCl4 is a wide-gap chloride that shares the Cl- anion with Li6PS5Cl, so it should avoid the P-O and S-O oxidation products that gave the oxides and phosphate their 0.29-0.34 eV/atom contact penalties. Its Zn2+ is harder to reduce than Li+ in the sulfide, so it may be chemically more compatible at the cathode interface than the oxide and fluoride coatings tested so far.

This points to the oxide and fluoride anions as the problem, so a chloride-based coating that matches the electrolyte anion is the next family to test.
